brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: Base built from 5 pieces: 3×full (0,0,0; 0,1,0; 1,0,0) and 2×half-s (-1,0,0; 1,1,0) forming connected platform, locked with jointBolts.

3 bins placed: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments), bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments), bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments); bins are drop-in removable. Staged with tweezers, multimeter etc.
Two drawers installed: drawer:0#-1,0#cut and drawer:0#1,1#cut on half-base cut faces.
handle:0,0,0;top installed on cover:0,0,0;full;top with 3 cover inserts (60°,180°,300° bearing). Covers on 3 full cells to support handle.

finish.summary: Built compact 3-cell full + 2 half-cell base with 3 removable compartment bins (8 compartments total), 2 drawers, and top-mounted carry handle. Joints locked; props show electronics use. Check_build meshClash clear.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
